summary.tldr: Requires dangerous offenders and people convicted of more than one first degree murder to be classified and confined as maximum security inmates.
what_it_does: Requires the Correctional Service to assign a maximum security classification to any inmate found to be a dangerous offender or convicted of more than one first degree murder.
Requires those inmates to be confined in a maximum security penitentiary or a maximum security area in a penitentiary.
Limits transfers for these inmates by making section 29 subject to the new maximum security rule.
Makes inmates classified as maximum security ineligible for an unescorted temporary absence.
Sets the bill to come into force three months after royal assent.
who_it_affects: People with multiple first-degree murder convictions
summary.background: The Corrections and Conditional Release Act lets the Service assign inmates maximum, medium or minimum security classifications. This bill adds a rule for certain inmates to be classified as maximum security.
